flaw: The requested done counter conflicts with the project's own standing decision on record three weeks ago — a running total of finished rows only grows and answers nothing without a window nobody agreed on — so the pipeline says that plainly, with the reason, in the same reply that would otherwise just start the work.
what_you_do_next: State the conflict in the reply that carries the decision sheet, then proceed on his word either way: the sheet is written, admission runs the route through task-admission.py to open exactly one row and its checkpoint (checkpoint.py new with the sheet verbatim), the three lines land in scripts/state-probe.sh, the observable outcome — state-probe.sh printing the counter — is verified against the sheet without the producer's self-report, the checkpoint and row close in that same step, and the result is shown with the three edit lines (what that part said before, what it says now, what was added) so he can disagree while undoing is still cheap. Nothing waits for his eye as a gate; if he objects after seeing it, that is a new fact and a new row, not a reopening.
reasoning: The execution reference makes writing the decision sheet the single moment to weigh whether the thing asked for is right, and names exactly this case: a goal that conflicts with a standing decision already on record gets stated plainly, with the reason, in the same reply that would otherwise just begin the work. The decision record's no-running-total is such a standing decision, and nothing since reopened it, so silence here would be the failure the document calls out — competence-looking silent agreement, skipping the one check only the pipeline, holding the fuller picture of what is already decided, can run. But the objection is not a stall: the pipeline proceeds once heard out, on the human's word either way, and the last clause of his message is an instruction Director already routed as accepted work. The size of the change argues for a small sheet, not for skipping it — a line with nothing behind it gets one word or goes, and a one-line fix needs no risk paragraph (risk here is one word: reversible). Because the instruction names a goal nothing already covers, it creates exactly one row through the one write door and opens a fresh checkpoint carrying the sheet verbatim, so a resumed window reads the file rather than this conversation. Closing follows the shown-result law: the verifier confirms the observable outcome, the checkpoint and row close in the same step, and his eye is never the gate on an ordinary buildable result — this is not one of the three cases rule 12/27 reserve for him, and a redefinition he ordered himself is executing his decision, not making it.
